messages:
sam: Heads-up — noticed gradual GPU memory drift on the kv-cache stress job (persistent chat workload). +600MB over ~8h even with cache eviction on. nvml top shows no obvious processes spawning.
anya: ugh. Is this fragmentation or a leak? any repro script we can run locally?
sam: I scripted a loop that loads/shrinks KV pages and issues repeated generations. attaching output snips below.
sam: ```bash
# repro loop
for i in {1..1000}; do
  python tests/repro/kv_cache_stress.py --seq 2048 --batch 1
  sleep 5
done
```
jorge: ran your loop for 2 hours. saw a slow heap high-water increase. nvprof snapshot attached to next message.
jorge: nvml output excerpt: ```
GPU 0: used 8.1 GiB -> 8.7 GiB -> 9.1 GiB
Processes: python(pid=1423) GPU 0 100%
```
liz: can you paste allocator free list stats? We recently changed workspace sizing defaults in v2.3. Might be leftover buffers pinned in workspace arenas.
sam: allocator debug dump (trimmed): ```
Arenas: 3
Arena[0]: allocated 4.2GiB, free_chunks: 12, largest_free: 32MiB
Arena[1]: allocated 2.8GiB, free_chunks: 3, largest_free: 1MiB
Arena[2]: allocated 1.0GiB, free_chunks: 0, largest_free: 0
Total reserved: 8.0GiB, unmapped: 400MiB
```
anya: that looks like fragmentation — arena 2 has no free chunks. If workspace allocator never returns whole pages back to OS, accumulation possible. Did you enable "return_unused_pages" in allocator config?
sam: no, tests used default which is false currently for perf reasons.
mike: hypothesis: kernel selection changes earlier this week switched a fused kernel path that increases temporary workspace peak slightly and triggers new arena allocations that don't get reclaimed. Could explain regression after the kernel-picker change.
perf-bot: perf alert: regression detected on main CI (latency +3% tail, mem high-water +~500MB) linked run: https://perf.redwood/rep/8821
jorge: I captured a timeline with CUPTI counters and a brief cudaMalloc/cudaFree trace. snippet: ```
malloc 0x7f.. 12.3MB
free 0x7f.. 12.3MB
malloc 0x8a.. 256MB
free 0x8a.. 0
# note: free reported 0 (not freed) until epoch boundary
```
liz: that 0 in free is suspicious. Could be our wrapper's deferred free queue not flushed on some codepaths (batching heuristic bypass). Any codepaths doing async_free without host sync?
sam: repro shows pattern tied to large attention windows + batch size 1 under streaming. If we toggle batching heuristic to favor larger micro-batches it reduces churn and mem stabilizes.
anya: can we try two quick mitigations: (1) enable return_unused_pages=true on allocator for a job run, (2) force periodic gc of deferred free queue in kv cache code?
sam: started a run with return_unused_pages=true and periodic flush every 10 minutes. update in ~45m.
jorge: shared small instrumented repro at gist: https://gist.github.com/jorge/kv-mem-drift (includes nvprof, allocator dumps, and run.sh)
mike: added extra logging for kernel-picker to see which kernels allocate large temp buffers. in my local replay I can reproduce increase when using the fused-attn kernel v3.2.
liz: action items: 1) run repro with return_unused_pages on (sam) 2) add forced flush of deferred frees in kv-cache path (anya/jorge) 3) re-run kernel selection A/B by pinning older kernel (mike) 4) add allocator guard that logs when free list shrinks to zero for an arena (liz)
sam: quick update — after enabling return_unused_pages the job kept memory stable for 2h, no slow drift visible. odds this is fragmentation + arenas not returned to OS.
perf-bot: note: enabling return_unused_pages increases peak alloc time ~2-3ms on first big allocation (seen in trace), but major leak gone.
deploy-bot: rolled a canary with return_unused_pages=true to dedicated-infer-02 for overnight run.
anya: still want the forced deferred-free flush as a safety net; will open PR today with toggle + unit test.
jorge: adding repro notes: include --force-kernel=fused-attn-v3.2 to stress path. Also attach a short profiler snapshot showing the temp buffers pinned across iterations.
mike: if PRs land we'll run long-run job 24h and compare high-water curves.
sam: thanks all — getting much closer. if nightly canary looks clean we'll promote default for workspace sizing. :+1:
